Both, in order: 1) a starter emergency fund (one month of bills), 2) any employer retirement match, 3) high-interest debt, 4) a full 3–6 month emergency fund, 5) then low-rate debt or bigger goals. The math: a 50% match beats even a 24% card, and a 24% card beats any savings account.

title: Your Credit Score, Explained in Numbers
desc:
A FICO score is five parts: payment history 35%, amounts owed 30%, length of history 15%, new credit 10%, credit mix 10%. The two that matter most: pay on time (autopay the minimum) and keep utilization low. The episode-one card goes from 64% utilization to under 30% by month 5. Checking your own score doesn't hurt it; free reports are at AnnualCreditReport.com.

title: Owe Taxes? How to Pay Without a Credit Card
desc:
Owe $2,400 in taxes? First, file on time even if you can't pay: the late-filing penalty is usually far bigger than the late-payment one. Then compare: a credit card at $450 a month costs about $215 in fees and interest; an IRS short-term payment plan costs about $86. Plus how to avoid owing next year.
